correctness.rationale: For every pair of disjoint edges, conditioning on their uniform weights yields a shared-comparator factor (1-max(x,y))^h, whose two ordered-domain integrals are 1/[a(a+b-h)] and 1/[b(a+b-h)]. Subtraction gives the exact covariance h/[ab(a+b-h)]. Intersecting edges are exclusive. A triangle-free d-regular host has m(d-1)^2 cross-edge witnesses and exactly 2c4 edge pairs with h=2, giving the advertised square correction after the adjacent-pair variance cancellation. All integer cases and boundary restrictions are accounted for; independent exact-rank enumeration plus rational checks printed 13598 assertions. The finite code is corroboration, not a universal proof.

value.rationale: The variance of the number of mutually chosen low-cost edges in a network distinguishes otherwise degree-identical triangle-free regular graphs by exactly the number of four-cycles. The coefficient is strictly positive and gives an iff girth-five baseline; this recovers a specific structural motif from a distribution-free randomized nearest-neighbor observable. Pairwise sign and induced-matching independence furnish the mechanism, not merely a restatement of one graph enumeration. This natural network invariant and exact classification meet the substantive mathematical-value threshold.
